newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-PENAROL OPEN UP SLENDER LEAD IN LIBERTADORES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PENAROL OPEN UP SLENDER LEAD IN LIBERTADORES.

text.p: Penarol, the once-great Uruguayan soccer club struggling to emerge from the doldrums, opened up a narrow lead in their Libertadores Cup quarter-final tie against Argentina's Racing Club on Wednesday.

Penarol, who have not reached this stage of the tournament for 10 years, won the first leg 1-0 at home in Montevideo to leave the tie finely balanced against another former power that has lost its way in recent years.
Defender Roberto Lima scored the winner in the 24th minute, following a corner in a game played on a near-waterlogged pitch.
Penarol have won the trophy five times but had failed to progress beyond the second round since their last win in 1987.
Last year, they were knocked out after a demoralising 5-1 home defeat by San Lorenzo of Argentina and they did not qualify at all years between 1990 and 1994.
Racing, Liberatadores champions in 1967 and one of the biggest clubs in Argentina, have not won a domestic title for 31 years.
The two other first legs played Wednesday also ended in single-goal wins for the home teams.

Bolivian champions Bolivar, with the advantage of playing at 3,700 metres above sea level in the mining town of Oruro, beat Peruvian champions Sporting Cristal 2-1 but missed a host of chances to increase their lead.
Eduardo Jiguchi opened the score for Boliviar with a penalty before halftime and Sergio Joao increasing the home team's lead in the 76th minute.
Luis Bonnet reduced the arrears for Cristal seven minutes from time when he slipped the ball under former Cameroon international goalkeeper Thomas N'Kono. Neither club has ever won the title.
Colo Colo, the only Chilean team ever to have lifted the trophy, were beaten 2-1 by compatriots and city rivals Universidad Catolica in Santiago.
Universidad's Argentine striker Alberto Acosta, who scored four goals in a game against Bolivia's Oriente Petrolero in the previous round, grabbed the winner.
The first leg of the remaining tie between Brazilian sides Cruzeiro and Gremio will be played on May 27, having been postponed because Gremio are in the final of a domestic competition this week.
